'''Claudine Hermann''' ({{Née|Rodrigues}}, 19 December 1945 &ndash; 17 July 2021) was a French [[physicist]] and honorary professor at [[École Polytechnique]], the [[grande école]] founded in 1794 and located in [[Palaiseau]], France. In 1992 she became the first woman to serve there as a professor. As a researcher, she has specialized in [[solid-state physics]]. She has also served as president of the [[European Platform of Women Scientists]] and in 2000 was one of several women who founded [[Femmes et Sciences]]. In early 2025, that organization proposed 72 names of women in science to be added to the sides of the Eiffel Tower, including Hermann herself.

== Biography ==

=== Early life and education ===
Claudine Rodrigues was the daughter of a pharmacist. She studied at the [[École normale supérieure de jeunes filles]] and graduated in 1965. In 1969, she passed the competitive [[agrégation]] examination in physics. The same year she married Jean-Paul Hermann whose career was similar to her own. By 1980, they had three children together.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.archicubes.ens.fr/lannuaire#annuaire_chercher?identite=Claudine+Hermann|title=L'annuaire {{!}} a-Ulm|website=www.archicubes.ens.fr|access-date=2018-12-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150520151458/http://www.archicubes.ens.fr/lannuaire#annuaire_chercher?identite=Claudine+Hermann|archive-date=2015-05-20|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://watermark02.silverchair.com/75_1_online.pdf?token=AQECAHi208BE49Ooan9kkhW_Ercy7Dm3ZL_9Cf3qfKAc485ysgAAAuYwggLiBgkqhkiG9w0BBwagggLTMIICzwIBADCCAsgGCSqGSIb3DQEHATAeBglghkgBZQMEAS4wEQQMXlov08jttTK9KyUYAgEQgIICmSb7L38KpLDMAm4s846Y7r4a6le3AhKlpzc3pc9ji7T0dMcOxYh5t2D2ICpseZDJngtoPHyY5ycKIsMWQJ3pLYvj9pK5HT_O-CeeTvbDQqzG3_3YpNVe4tDryrdw9YnTuX6zmAXG63EdfqcS7aJ0ZffVfsDLiJlFaxhp6TdYM4UubeIp03i58DGMhYKDWsesSJZG2p8seTFr6ZeIFOMeInlJbtOOvhFUJbvyFLEZl_9D4lWPUNB1FaatZ20ONCeegCmIn7FINfwEM-ISl71uZNkohEGRew3Pv2dnx5K7sN5uHBFo4Ru9EA1OhHTUN-6bN9MaWls4sQKiwPaU2WBoopaHjxiZ8ciXCphQLHn-yxZ2cxfNHWtPLl_o3ur4kfjZik7yPjOKjRe9B4AWeQZRaJYjOSanuiVUvGbnxy4Cwb2SQqwlNEnlTMogAbK63XsVB8lrMVloZEgIIh8FFPsfrzB7HgmJPIAR9WV4AWWaCSNWQxaXRYouDLf7hsMNwhxjIVFq7e-kvZ4DC5FhXkcWp6sSzu8c51uiAYc4y1oMAPkt48cDrb04JcJSu3dJ3avF7h9Dvmy4DuX9GMo8C4S-KkXCDpGJE9dtSMPll8C0kkBMXuYhbiZ_IhpD2NLXhQMAqiUwMazAV4Dj5dpK6jud5yKYdUJt_QPzs8Q0dBbDGsY7FbNjCpaSKbFDtBYGvh0ASES3puTkBp7JnN3aL7xpcSDh9bsPPVoga3W_SPGNUijKivKhpvH8RCFWfP1mQgHECewG_P7mCqfVgZx3Ynvzfk2mTIAyVFUCGmFOoo32Ybgo0X6y_DL-WmBkpaM64PMEiKtzAk0Uyx5mVxdEitW9cZFuqyCircqN2s0EZgdMfO1Ezx_Y_1WTJHHC|title=The European Commission Report on Women and Science, and One Frenchwoman's Experience|author=Hermann, Claudine|publisher=AIP Publishing|year=2002|access-date=16 July 2026}}</ref><ref name=vni/><ref>{{Cite web |title=RODRIGUES Claudine (épouse HERMANN) - She completed her doctoral studies at [[Paris Diderot University]] in 1976, with a thesis titled "Pompage optique dans l'antimoniure de gallium : détection optique de la résonance électronique" (Optical pumping in [[gallium antimonide]]: optical detection of electron resonance).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://lucienne.ens.psl.eu/s/lucienne/item/264226|title=Hernaamm, Claudine|publisher=Lucienne|access-date=16 July 2026|language=French}}</ref><ref>{{Cite thesis|last=Hermann|first=Claudine|title=Pompage optique dans l'antimoniure de gallium: détection optique de la résonance électronique|date=1976|degree=Thèse. Sc. phys. Paris VI. 1976|publisher=Paris VI.|url=http://www.sudoc.abes.fr/xslt/DB=2.1//SRCH?IKT=12&TRM=00878941X&COOKIE=U10178,Klecteurweb,I250,B341720009+,SY,NLECTEUR+WEBOPC,D2.1,Ebc67e8ec-4,A,H,R130.246.255.98,FY&COOKIE=U10178,Klecteurweb,I250,B341720009+,SY,NLECTEUR+WEBOPC,D2.1,Ebc67e8ec-4,A,H,R208.80.154.49,FY|place=Paris, pays inconnu}}</ref> In 1977 she published the obtained value of the [[Landé g-factor]] ''g''=-0.44 for electrons in [[gallium arsenide]], which is important for spin physics in the [[Quantum Hall effect|quantum Hall regime]].<ref name=":2" />

=== Research and career ===
Hermann was appointed a lecturer at [[École Polytechnique]] in 1980.<ref name=vni>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vousnousils.fr/2007/04/06/claudine-hermann-une-femme-enseignante-a-polytechnique-238453|title=Claudine Hermann, une femme enseignante à Polytechnique » VousNousIls|date=2007-04-06|website=VousNousIls|language=fr-FR|access-date=2018-12-14|archive-date=2018-12-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181215065925/https://www.vousnousils.fr/2007/04/06/claudine-hermann-une-femme-enseignante-a-polytechnique-238453|url-status=dead}}</ref> She taught classes in semiconductor physics.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|url=https://www.springer.com/gb/book/9780387940243|title=Physics of Semiconductors|last1=Sapoval|first1=B.|last2=Hermann|first2=C.|date=1995|publisher=Springer-Verlag|isbn=9780387940243|location=New York|language=en}}</ref> She worked on the optical properties of solids, in particular the photo-emission of polarised electrons.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.acceleratingera.vu.lt/speakers/item/18-claudine-hermann|title=Accelerating ERA development|website=Accelerating Era Development|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-12-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://socialmetwork.blog/tag/science/|title=science – The Social Metwork|date=6 February 2018 |language=en|access-date=2018-12-14}}</ref> She developed techniques to optically measure the spin resonance in semiconductors.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hermann|first1=Claudine|last2=Lampel|first2=Georges|date=1971-08-16|title=Measurement of the g Factor of Conduction Electrons by Optical Detection of Spin Resonance in p-Type Semiconductors|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=27|issue=7|pages=373–376|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.27.373|bibcode=1971PhRvL..27..373H}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last1=Weisbuch|first1=Claude|last2=Hermann|first2=Claudine|date=1977-01-15|title=Optical detection of conduction-electron spin resonance in <math>{\mathrm{Ga}}\mathrm{As}</math>, <math>{\mathrm{Ga}}_{1-x}{\mathrm{In}}_{x}\mathrm{As}</math>, and <math>{\mathrm{Ga}}_{1-x}{\mathrm{Al}}_{x}\mathrm{As}</math>|journal=Physical Review B|volume=15|issue=2|pages=816–822|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.15.816}}</ref>  She demonstrated the hole effective mass (0.051) of [[indium gallium arsenide]] in 1981.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hermann|first1=Claudine|last2=Pearsall|first2=Thomas P.|year=1981|title=Optical pumping and the valence-band light-hole effective mass in GaInAsP|journal=Applied Physics Letters|volume=38|issue=6|pages=450–452|doi=10.1063/1.92393|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Hermann was the first woman to be appointed Professor at the École Polytechnique in 1992.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://educationandgenderequality.com/claudine-hermann/|title=Claudine Hermann|last=consulatboston|date=2017-06-15|website=Education and Gender Equality - International Symposium|language=en-US|access-date=2018-12-14}}</ref> She spent a year as a visiting researcher at [[Nagoya University]] in Japan in 1998.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.vbl.nagoya-u.ac.jp/e/activities/activities.html|title=Research Activities|website=www.vbl.nagoya-u.ac.jp|access-date=2018-12-14}}</ref>

=== Activism ===
Thanks to her connection with [[Huguette Delavault]], she developed a strong interest in women scientists in France. She was startled to find that at the École Polytechnique, only 15% of the students were women. This observation led her to attend conferences and write papers on promoting the role of women in the area of science.<ref name="vni" />

In the year 2000, together with [[Françoise Cyrot-Lackmann]], Huguette Delavault, [[Françoise Gaspard]], [[Colette Kreder]] and the [[Femmes et Mathématiques]] association, Hermann was behind the creation of [[Femmes et Sciences]], an organization designed to encourage girls and women to participate in science. In early 2025, it proposed that the names of 72 women in science should be added to the Eiffel Tower.<ref name=frgap>{{Cite web |title=France Addresses Gender Gap in Science |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/france-addresses-gender-gap-science |access-date=2026-06-10 |website=www.science.org |language=en}}</ref>

Alongside her research into condensed matter, Hermann worked to make the environment better for women physicists.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.archicubes.ens.fr/espace-carri%C3%A8res/portrait-du-mois/claudine-hermann|title=Claudine Hermann {{!}} a-Ulm|website=www.archicubes.ens.fr|access-date=2018-12-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.friendsofeurope.org/publication/breaking-glass-ceiling-women-and-girls-science|website=www.friendsofeurope.org|access-date=2018-12-14|title=Breaking the glass ceiling for women and girls in science &#124; Friends of Europe|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181215065929/https://www.friendsofeurope.org/publication/breaking-glass-ceiling-women-and-girls-science|archive-date=2018-12-15|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1999 she was appointed to the [[European Union]] [[The Helsinki Group on Women in Science|Helsinki Group]] on women and science, and remained a member until 2006.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lajauneetlarouge.com/auteur/claudine-hermann|title=Claudine HERMANN {{!}} La Jaune et la Rouge|website=www.lajauneetlarouge.com|access-date=2018-12-14}}</ref> She co-founded the platform [[Femmes et Sciences]] with [[Huguette Delavault]] in 2000''.''<ref name=":0" /> She was a member of the expert group who produced the European Technology Assessment Network (ETAN) report on women in academia - ''Science Policies in the European Union: promoting excellence through mainstreaming gender equality'' ''-'' for the [[European Union]] in 2000.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Rees |first=Teresa |date=September 2001 |title=Mainstreaming Gender Equality in Science in the European Union: The 'ETAN Report' |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/09540250120063544 |journal=Gender and Education |language=en |volume=13 |issue=3 |pages=243–260 |doi=10.1080/09540250120063544 |issn=0954-0253|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=EPWS |date=2021-07-21 |title=Prof. Claudine Hermann – EPWS Honorary President 2021 |url=https://epws.org/prof-claudine-hermann-epws-honorary-president-2021/ |access-date=2026-07-16 |website=European Platform of Women Scientists EPWS |language=en-US}}</ref>

Hermann was President of the [[European Platform of Women Scientists]] from 2017-2021,<ref name=":3" /> and was elected also the President of Honour of the EPWS in 2021, shortly before her death.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://expertes.fr/expertes/66640-claudine-hermann|title=Claudine Hermann|website=Expertes France|language=fr-FR|access-date=2018-12-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=EPWS |date=2022-07-17 |title=Dear Claudine, women scientists will always remember you! |url=https://epws.org/dear-claudine-women-scientists-will-always-remember-you/ |access-date=2026-07-16 |website=European Platform of Women Scientists EPWS |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last=Citoyennes pour l'Europe|title=Claudine Hermann: Europe of Women Scientists|date=12 March 2018 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HGiCmjiXVUU|access-date=2018-12-14}}</ref>

=== Death ===
Claudine Hermann, aged 76, passed away on 17 July 2021, in a struggle against cancer.<ref>{{Cite web |last=EPWS |date=2021-07-21 |title=Prof. Claudine Hermann, EPWS Honorary President 2021, passed away |url=https://epws.org/professor-claudine-hermann-epws-honorary-president-2021-passed-away/ |access-date=2026-06-20 |website=European Platform of Women Scientists EPWS |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Honours and awards ==
* 2015 Grand Officer of the [[Legion of Honour]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.legiondhonneur.fr/sites/default/files/promotion/lh_20150101.pdf|website=www.legiondhonneur.fr|access-date=2018-12-14|title=JOURNAL OFFICIEL DE LA RÉPUBLIQUE FRANÇAISE Présidence de la République ORDRE NATIONAL DE LA LÉGION D’HONNEUR Décret du 31 décembre 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.femmesetsciences.fr/actualites/claudine-hermann-decoree-par-le-president-francois-hollande/|title=Claudine Hermann, décorée par le Président François Hollande {{!}} Association Femmes & Sciences|last=Secretaire|first=A. propos de l’auteur|language=fr-FR|access-date=2018-12-14|archive-date=2020-10-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201020171659/https://www.femmesetsciences.fr/actualites/claudine-hermann-decoree-par-le-president-francois-hollande/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last=FemmesetSciences|title=Discours du Président-Remise de décoration Claudine Hermann-20 mai 2015|date=25 May 2015 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xs80oCKVNnw|access-date=2018-12-14}}</ref>
* 2010 [[National Order of Merit (France)|Grand Officer of the National Order of Merit]]
On 8 March 2024, [[Sorbonne Paris North University|Université Sorbonne Paris Nord]] in [[Villetaneuse]] renamed one of its lecture theatres the “Claudine-Hermann Lecture Theatre” in Hermann's memory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ferbos |first=Léa |date=2024-02-09 |title=Journée Femmes et sciences |url=https://www.univ-spn.fr/journee-femmes-et-sciences/ |access-date=2026-07-16 |website=Université Sorbonne Paris Nord |language=fr-FR}}</ref> The same year a secondary school in [[Massy, Essonne|Massy]] was named after her.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Collège Claudine Hermann - 46 rue de Vilgenis, 91300 Massy |url=https://clg-hermann-massy.ac-versailles.fr/spip.php?article1 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250329044812/https://clg-hermann-massy.ac-versailles.fr/spip.php?article1 |archive-date=2025-03-29 |access-date=2026-07-16 |website=clg-hermann-massy.ac-versailles.fr |language=fr}}</ref>

In 2026, Hermann was announced as one of 72 historical women in STEM whose names have been proposed to be added to the [[List of the 72 names on the Eiffel Tower|72 men]] already celebrated on the [[Eiffel Tower]]. The plan was announced by the Mayor of Paris, [[Anne Hidalgo]] following the recommendations of a committee led by [[Isabelle Vauglin]] of [[Femmes et Sciences|Femmes et sciences]] and Jean-François Martins, representing the operating company which runs the Eiffel Tower.<ref name="sp">{{Cite web |title=Eiffel Tower: a list of 72 women scientists will soon be inscribed on the Parisian monument |url=https://www.sortiraparis.com/en/news/in-paris/articles/340564-eiffel-tower-list-of-72-women-scientists-soon-to-be-honored-on-the-paris-landmark |access-date=2026-02-05 |website=www.sortiraparis.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Les noms des 72 femmes pour la Tour Eiffel ont été révélés. |url=https://www.femmesetsciences.fr/news/les-noms-des-72-femmes-pour-la-tour-eiffel-ont-%C3%A9t%C3%A9-r%C3%A9v%C3%A9l%C3%A9 |access-date=2026-06-26 |website=Femmes & Sciences |language=fr}}</ref><ref>[https://10ca8303-b3dc-4a91-9dcc-2d2b91792b47.usrfiles.com/ugd/10ca83_3838bd19a41a4e83927cfc8fe0f50404.pdf 72 femmes de sciences pour la tour Eiffel] ''Femmes & Sciences'' (in French). Retrieved 2026-06-26</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-01-26 |title=Eiffel Tower to honor 72 women scientists for posterity |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/france/article/2026/01/26/eiffel-tower-to-honor-72-women-in-science-for-posterity_6749828_7.html |access-date=2026-02-05 |language=en}}</ref>
